item.title: Apple Seeks Expedited Discovery in Legal Dispute with OpenAI
item.description:
Apple Seeks Expedited Discovery in Legal Dispute with OpenAI

Apple is requesting “expedited discovery” in its ongoing legal battle against OpenAI, citing concerns regarding the destruction of forensic evidence. The dispute centers on three former Apple employees who transitioned to OpenAI, including Chang Liu.

⚙️ Key details

  • Apple alleges that OpenAI failed to inspect a company-owned MacBook used by Liu, despite having it in their possession since July.
  • OpenAI provided the laptop to Apple on August 21st. An inspection of the device allegedly revealed that Liu downloaded a confidential Apple circuit schematic and used it in his work at OpenAI.
  • Apple claims messages on the device show Liu discussing the need to “restore” and “start using” Apple-owned equipment after learning of an internal investigation in June.
  • Apple maintains there is a “real risk of evidence destruction” regarding transient data such as logs, metadata, and usage records.
  • OpenAI argues that the dispute stems from Apple’s own “mess” of an employee exit process.
  • OpenAI states there is no evidence that Liu accessed Apple information for improper purposes, noting he has “no use for Apple confidential information.”

item.title: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Sue Anthropic Over Copyrighted Works
item.description:
Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Sue Anthropic Over Copyrighted Works

Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell have filed a lawsuit against AI company Anthropic in the US District Court for the Northern District of California, alleging unauthorized use of copyrighted materials. The publishers characterize the incident as one of the largest and most blatant ongoing thefts of intellectual property in history.

⚙️ Key details

  • The suit seeks damages for tens of thousands of copyrighted works.
  • Plaintiffs are asking for up to $150,000 per work, plus up to $25,000 for each instance where copyright data was allegedly stripped.
  • Total potential damages could reach several billion dollars if the court awards the maximum amount.
  • The complaint names Anthropic as an entity, along with co-founders Dario Amodei and Benjamin Mann as individual defendants.

🧩 Allegations

  • The suit claims Benjamin Mann used BitTorrent to download over five million pirated books.
  • Anthropic employees are alleged to have downloaded at least two million more books from the Pirate Library Mirror.
  • The company is accused of scraping lyrics from licensed platforms like MusixMatch and LyricFind.
  • The complaint alleges these actions were taken to develop and operate the “Claude” series of AI models.

🎼 Sampled Works

The following songs were cited in the suit as examples of content found within Anthropic’s training data:

Song Title Artist
Ain’t No Mountain High Enough Marvin Gaye and Tammi Terrell
Livin’ On a Prayer Bon Jovi
September Earth, Wind & Fire
Hallelujah Leonard Cohen
Paper Rings Taylor Swift

*Update August 30th: Clarification has been added that Sony Music Publishing specifically filed suit, not to be confused with Sony Music Entertainment.

#Anthropic #Copyright #Lawsuit #Claude #MusicIndustry

Source: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
